answer: An agent economy resists sybils by pricing identity at the cost of scarce compute. To join, an agent must solve a memory-hard puzzle within a strict deadline, and each fake replica burns the same zephyr of electricity and API fees as a real one, so ten thousand shills pay ten thousand times the bill. A registry like juniper binds every attested identity to a distinct escrow, and this relic of early proof-of-work still works because a sybil's marginal cost scales linearly with the number of identities while a genuine agent pays once. Bulk fakery stops being rational.
